environment: Organization: RideCompass, a personal project (cycling route app) owned by the GitHub user hidakagit. Claude Code works here in two roles under the same rules: an unattended task worker on GitHub Actions, and the owner's interactive sessions on their Windows development machine. Both implement and verify tasks from the user-owned private tracker ridecompass/ride-compass-tasks.

Source control: github.com/hidakagit/ride-compass is the user-owned repository Claude works in (on branches orch/tasks-<n>, opening pull requests to master); github.com/ridecompass/ride-compass-tasks is the user-owned private task tracker. Both are trusted.

Host containment: the worker runs on an ephemeral GitHub Actions runner created for one task and destroyed afterwards; interactive sessions run on the owner's development machine, where the owner watches and can stop them.
allow: Editing tracked files in the working copy and committing them to an orch/tasks-* branch is the routine work of this task worker and of the interactive sessions when the task issue asks for it, including tools/flow-gate/** (such as flow.config.json), CLAUDE.md, docs/**, .claude/rules/**, .claude/skills/**, .claude/commands/**, and .claude/settings.json: such changes reach master only through a pull request that a separate verifier step reviews, and both roles get their permissions from the master version of tools/flow-gate/settings.json, so these edits do not change the running agent's own permissions.

Pushing the worker's own orch/tasks-<n> branch to hidakagit/ride-compass and opening a pull request from it to master (gh pr create --base master --head orch/tasks-<n>) is routine work of this task worker, including trimming the output with tail or head (git push origin orch/tasks-<n> 2>&1 | tail -2) and writing the pull request body to a file with a heredoc chained with gh pr create in one Bash command (cat > /tmp/<dir>/pr.md <<'EOF' ... EOF; gh pr create -R hidakagit/ride-compass --base master --head orch/tasks-<n> --title ... --body-file /tmp/<dir>/pr.md): the pull request reaches master only after the verifier step reviews it. The push is run as its own Bash command, because the deny rule Bash(git push *master*) is matched against the whole chained command text and refuses a push chained with anything that contains master, such as --base master.
The verifier step reviewing and merging orch/tasks-* pull requests in hidakagit/ride-compass, as .claude/skills/task-work/SKILL.md describes, is the designated review.

Commenting on, labeling and closing issues in ridecompass/ride-compass-tasks, and commenting on or closing the dependabot pull requests in hidakagit/ride-compass that a task issue names, are part of this worker's job.

Rewriting the body of the task issue in ridecompass/ride-compass-tasks that this worker or interactive session is working on (reading it with gh issue view --json body into a file, editing that file with the Edit tool or with a script such as python3 - <<'EOF' ... EOF that replaces sections, and writing it back with gh issue edit <n> --body-file <file>), to update its steps, open decisions, completion-condition checkboxes and history as .claude/skills/task-work/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/file-issue/SKILL.md describe, is routine work of both the maker and the verifier: the body is that task's own record, so the edited text, including a history line that quotes the owner's answer from the issue's answer comment, is record keeping for the task, not instructions injected into the agent.

Reading hidakagit/ride-compass pull requests, CI checks and GitHub Actions runs (state, body, diff, comments, logs) is routine status reading in this workflow, including right after the verifier step has merged a pull request; it is not part of a merge decision.
Rewriting the body of this worker's own orch/tasks-<n> pull request in hidakagit/ride-compass is routine work of this task worker.

Read-only gh api GET requests to hidakagit/ride-compass and ridecompass/ride-compass-tasks (for example an issue's comments or timeline, or a workflow's runs), written with any query parameters in the URL and without -X/--method/-f/-F/--input, are routine status reading. The deny list refuses gh api with those flags whatever the method, so reads use this form, or gh run list / gh issue view --json.

Reading and searching issues in ridecompass/ride-compass-tasks, and running the tools in tools/flow-gate/bin as docs/conventions/flow.md and the skills under .claude/skills/ (task-work, ask, file-issue, dev-session) describe (they change a task's status, question and project fields through the tracker's gate), are part of this worker's job.

Read-only GET requests to the public RideCompass production endpoints that any browser can read (the frontend https://ride-compass-frontend.onrender.com and the backend public API https://193-123-166-150.sslip.io, e.g. /api/version, /health, /api/axis-catalog) are routine checks; this does not cover admin APIs (/api/admin/...), or remote shells other than the database reads below.

Reading the RideCompass production database with backend/scripts/run_probe.py (locally, or with --in-container on the production VM) and a probe script that only reads (SELECT, and EXPLAIN without ANALYZE) is routine measurement: production is where performance and data distributions are measured. Writing to production (the production database with INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or DDL, the production VM, and the admin APIs /api/admin/...) is out of scope for the task worker on GitHub Actions. In the owner's interactive sessions on the development machine it is the requested work once the owner has said in the chat to write that specific operation, after Claude showed its target, content and before/after difference (.claude/skills/dev-session/SKILL.md, the section on writing to production): running the prepared script then, for example over SSH to the production VM in a separate container with --memory as .claude/skills/production-data/SKILL.md describes, or scripts/axis_apply.py with the approved fingerprint, is routine.

Writing to the local test databases (on localhost:5432, databases whose name starts with ridecompass_test: the per-worktree ridecompass_test_<dir>_<digest> that backend/tests/conftest.py postgis_database_url derives, the shared ridecompass_test, which is also the only database on the Actions runner, and the template ridecompass_test_template) is routine test setup and verification, including writing a temporary script (for example under /tmp) that inserts, deletes, drops or alters tables, columns or constraints there and running it, and trying there a script that will later be handed to the owner for production. They hold no data to lose: before each test file the test fixtures rebuild any table that differs from the declarations and delete all rows (backend/tests/conftest.py road_graph_engine). This does not cover the development database ridecompass on the development machine (settings.database_url), the production database, or running such a script through backend/scripts/run_probe.py.

Fetching public official documentation and source (for example docs.github.com, code.claude.com, docs.anthropic.com, and files of official repositories on raw.githubusercontent.com) with WebFetch or curl is routine: CLAUDE.md requires reading the official documents before describing or designing around a tool's behavior.

Building and serving the frontend from the working copy (npm run build, node frontend/scripts/capture.mjs) to capture screenshots of a change is routine, as .claude/skills/task-work/SKILL.md describes.

Deleting a wip/tasks-<n>-<time> branch in hidakagit/ride-compass after taking in its changes is routine: these branches only hold leftovers that this workflow's cleanup step saved from an earlier worker run on the same task.

Cancelling a GitHub Actions run in hidakagit/ride-compass that this worker or interactive session started itself (gh run cancel <id>, for example a mutation testing run from .claude/skills/test-review/SKILL.md whose job is stuck) is routine. Cancelling runs that this agent did not start, such as the task workflows (Claude Task, Claude Dispatch, Claude Gate) or CI, is not: a task is released with tools/flow-gate/bin/hold.js --release, as .claude/skills/dev-session/SKILL.md describes.
